summary: @whalent/agent ships an obfuscated daemon that executes remote gateway commands as shell/PTY/Jupyter code on the installer host
details: The package installs a daemon (`whalent`) whose documented behavior is to connect to a WebSocket gateway (default a vendor-controlled endpoint, overridable via `--gateway`) and accept remote commands including `upgrade` and `restart`. Runtime dependencies include `node-pty`, `ssh2`, `@xterm/headless`, and `ws`, and the shipped Python sidecar `dist/jupyter_sidecar.py` implements an `execute` RPC that calls `jupyter_client.execute(code)` on caller-supplied code strings. Any party controlling the configured gateway can drive PTY/shell sessions and execute arbitrary Python cells on the machine running the agent, i.e. full remote code execution against the host. Both `dist/index.cjs` (128 KB) and `dist/core.cjs` (13 MB) are shipped as javascript-obfuscator output: hex-named identifiers (`_0x...`), control-flow flattening, and a rotating string-array decoder with 106,660 entries; `javascript-obfuscator` is a declared devDependency. The obfuscation prevents inspection of how gateway-supplied messages are dispatched to the PTY/SSH/Jupyter execution primitives. Because command execution requires the operator to start the daemon with a token/gateway, install-time auto-exec is not present, but the daemon-startup exposure is a hidden-remote-execution surface controlled by whoever holds the gateway.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
